title: Architecture & Design Review Board (ARB) Governance Framework for a Workspace Transformation
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Give the transformation a decision authority that sticks
problem: Large transformations drift when there's no forum with the authority to approve designs and stop bad ones. This solution stands up an Architecture & Design Review Board (ARB) for a Google Workspace + Gemini program: charter, decision rights, review gates, submission templates, and a design-drift-prevention process — so every major design decision is reviewed against the target architecture and vendor execution stays aligned to enterprise standards.
whats_inside: Governance Overview — the ARB's mandate, scope, and how it relates to the target architecture and the workstreams.
Charter & Decision Rights — membership, quorum, decision authority (who approves what), escalation, and the boundary between vendor execution and enterprise architectural authority.

Review Gates & Templates — the stage gates (migration wave plans, identity/sync models, security configs, data-migration patterns, work-transformation approaches), submission templates, review checklists, and decision records.
5 supporting scripts — design-inventory discovery, conformance validation against approved standards, a decision/gap register report, safe remediation tracking, and a scope helper.
Drift-prevention process & a Design-Review-Board runbook — how to detect and stop unmanaged vendor-driven design drift, plus Testing gates and Best Practices.
short: Stand up an Architecture & Design Review Board for the transformation — charter, decision rights, review gates, templates, and drift prevention — so every major design is approved against the target architecture. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
